newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MATCHES THIS WEEKEND IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES THIS WEEKEND IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: The following matches are being played in the Spanish league championship this weekend: (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times GMT)
Saturday:
Tenerife (8) v Real Sociedad (6) kickoff 1930 gmt

Tenerife have lost former Real striker Meho Kodro, with a leg injury, as well as several key defenders ahead of a fixture that they have won in each of the past three seasons. Real have Romanian striker Gheorghe Craioveanu back from injury.
Sunday:
Athletic Bilbao (9) v Celta Vigo (13) 1600
Athletic have lost their goal touch in the past few games after star striker Julen Guerrero ran out of steam but they have only ever lost once at home to Celta, who have yet to find their form.
Valladolid (7) v Deportivo Coruna (3) 1600
After back-to-back defeats in the league and Cup Deportivo badly need to bounce back to take their first win at Valladolid, who will be without key Croatian striker Alen Peternac.
Valencia (11) v Rayo Vallecano (12) 1600

New Valencia coach Jorge Valdano has failed in his bid to find reinforcements in the transfer market and will have to use home-grown talent to deal with a Rayo side that continues to surprise, particularly away from home.
Extremadura (22) v Real Madrid (1) 1600
Real may be without Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos for a top-against-bottom clash which is likely to prove one of the most one-sided games in Europe over the weekend.
Sevilla (20) v Oviedo (14) 1600

Sevilla have only one league win at home and are wracked by board-room scandal but they were boosted earlier in the week by a Cup victory over Deportivo. Oviedo will be without star striker Oli Alvarez, the top Spanish goalscorer this season.
Logrones (18) v Espanyol (15) 1600
Identical poor records for both teams -- each side has just one win and a draw from their last seven games. But Espanyol start as favourites after a 4-1 midweek Cup victory.
Compostela (16) v Racing Santander (10) 1600
Compostela beat Espanyol convincingly last weekend but have not won at home since the second game of the season, while Racing tend to be at their best away from home.
Atletico Madrid (5) v Zaragoza (20) 1600

Atletico are unbeaten in nine matches but will be without suspended midfielder Diego Simeone for the game with Zaragoza who have newly-signed German goalkeeper Otto Konrad to help them try to halt a run of three successive league defeats
Sporting Gijon ((17) v Real Betis (4) 1830

After a 4-1 Cup defeat midweek, coach Benito Floro needs to add to Sporting's solitary home victory against a Betis side, who are unbeaten away but have been hit by influenza which has striker Alfonso Perez and four other players doubtful.
Monday:
Barcelona (2) v Hercules (21) 2030

With Brazilian prodigy Ronaldo back on form and compatriot Giovanni back from injury Barcelona fans will be hoping for a goal-feast in what promises to be one of the most unequal clashes of the season.
